To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the magnetic susceptibility (MS)-based proxies of Fe(III) and Fe(II)/ Fe(III) ratios and diatom assemblages reveal 1‐to‐2 ky long climatic extremes at 110‐, 103, and 90‐ky BP, which were contemporaneous with the discharges of North‐Atlantic and Arctic icebergs, documenting a teleconnection of the North Atlantic Ocean with East Central Siberia.

(1) the magnetic susceptibility of the sedimentary record from Lake Baikal is a good proxy for the reconstruction of the environmental changes in East Central Siberia; (2) the magnetic susceptibility is a good indicator of the changes in Fe mineralogy of the sediments, which is controlled by changes in lake water chemistry and the intensity of the biological processes in the lake.

the environmental record in the Lake Baikal sedimets is characterized by the following: (1) a dramatic climatic deterioration at 66–60 ky BP; (2) 1–2 ky long environmental changes at 110,103, 90-85, 77-60, 54,36, 27-23 and 19 ky B.P.

the study of the magnetic properties of rocks and sediments and their application to the investigation of the Earth’s past magnetic field and environmental changes.
the reconstruction of the environmental changes of the past in Lake Baikal, Siberia.
the reconstruction of the environmental conditions in the last 200 thousand years in Lake Baikal.

the magnetic susceptibility and diffuse reflectance spectral proxies are useful for paleoenvironmental reconstructions in Lake Baikal.

the magnetic susceptibility and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy are very powerful tools for reconstructing the paleoenvironmental changes in the Lake Baikal sedi-ments, especially in the absence of diatoms and pollen.
the DRS-based proxy of Fe(II)/(Fe(III) + Fe(II)) ratios in the mineral fraction of Lake Baikal sedi-ments is an effective tool for paleoenvironmental studies.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the inorganic proxies of MS and DSR are valuable for reconstructing paleoenvironmental changes in East Central Siberia.

the DRS and MS-based proxies of the Fe-bearing mineral assemblage provide an important record of paleoenvironmental changes in Lake Baikal, which can be correlated to other paleoclimate archives in Siberia and the Northern Hemisphere.
the magnetic susceptibility and the diffuse reflectance spectra provide valuable information on the paleoenvironmental history of the last 160 kyr.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the magnetic susceptibility and diffuse reflectance spectroscopy can be used to reconstruct paleoenvironments and that these proxies provide an additional tool for the interpretation of the paleoenvironmental record.
the DRS-based proxies are useful tools to reconstruct environmental changes in Lake Baikal.
the magnetic susceptibility and diffuse reflectance records are very useful for reconstructing environmental changes.
